about: Written by hand from CLAUDE.md and the crates' own docs. generate.py checks that every workspace package has an entry, with a layer that exists and a kind it knows, and that no entry names a package that is gone. layers: the rows of the map, top to bottom: where in the system a crate sits. Each crate: its layer; its kind, what sort of crate it is, checked by kinds.py; its concern in plain words; and what it must not do. A crate's must_not is given only where CLAUDE.md states one.

layers.title: Programs
layers.about: What runs: the kkt command, and the dev-only programs that assemble the same crates another way.

layers.title: Assembly
layers.about: Putting the server together from its parts.

layers.title: Surfaces
layers.about: What callers reach over HTTP: the MCP endpoints, their text, and the web page.

layers.title: Access
layers.about: Who is let in at all, who a caller is once in, and which host names the server answers to.

layers.title: Core
layers.about: Every decision and change, and the notices they send.

layers.title: Data
layers.about: The store and the database under it.

layers.title: Operations
layers.about: What is specific to running kkt on a machine: setup, settings, services, Docker, client configs, diagnostics, backups, lane files and the record of a server run.

layers.title: Clients
layers.about: kkt as a client of a server: the shared MCP client and `kkt watch`.

layers.title: Platform
layers.about: General crates that know nothing of kkt and would make sense in any program: time, randomness, logs, files, HTTP serving, the terminal, the browser, remote access, git and more. The test: a platform crate depends on no crate outside the platform layer.

layers.title: Dev-only
layers.about: Never in a release: test scratch folders.

kashkeshet.title: kkt (package kashkeshet)
kashkeshet.concern: The `kkt` command and everything it does on a machine: its subcommands and the files and environment they read, the settings and config file, the setup record, key files, how a client reaches the server, and one module per command that takes plain inputs. The agents' commands run in kkt-agent-commands, over the `AgentParts` it builds.
kashkeshet.must_not: Hold a clap type outside `cli.rs`, or let a command take one.

kkt-keymode.concern: A second program that assembles key mode again from the shared crates with none of the `kkt` program's code, to show the crates are a core and `kkt` one product on it. The HTTP-only end-to-end tests run against it in CI. Dev-only, never released.
kkt-keymode.must_not: Be released, or share code with the `kkt` program.

kkt-fake-product.concern: The shared crates assembled as a product other than kkt would assemble them, with two swarms and a fake `Identify` mapping made-up bearers to (swarm, role). Its tests check that nothing of one swarm reaches the other. Dev-only, never released.

kkt-webapp-preview.concern: The web page over simulated data, for working on the page: kkt-web's page over kkt-api-sim's simulated application and stand-in gate, with the real clock, randomness and stop signals, served alone through kkt-server and kkt-listen. Its flags and their checks (`SettingError`). Dev-only, never released.

kkt-operate.concern: The operator's commands, including the install's lifecycle (status, upgrade, uninstall and backup), and this machine's setup record and key selection; effects, backup writing and lazy serving facts are supplied through OperateParts.
kkt-operate.must_not: Choose native implementations, depend on an effect or another assembly, or parse command-line flags.

kkt-server.concern: Assembling the server around the program's `Arc<dyn AdminApi>` in `Parts`: `/mcp`, `/mcp-admin` and the web page; its `ServerSettings` returns an opaque `CheckedSettings` snapshot for `Parts::new` and composes owner checks and run-record lines with the program's plain values, with `SettingError`; the public adapter from admission and identity to the web gate; the page's sessions; the web page alone over its API and gate (`page`).
kkt-server.must_not: Make decisions: it only wires parts together. It does not choose who a caller is; the program passes `Identify` and the admission modes in.

kkt-mcp.concern: The agent and admin MCP tools, what the two share, their HTTP transport, and what agents are told about each tool.
kkt-mcp.must_not: Touch the database except through the rules, hold tool text in Rust, or decide who a caller is except through `Identify`.

kkt-web.concern: The human's pages, over the operator's operations (kkt-api-operator's `OperatorApi`) in each viewer's swarm, rendering the kkt-api crates' records. Its own contract is only `Gate`, which says who is viewing each request (a swarm and an operator) and whom a key signs in; every change is a checked form post. It keeps the limits only the page applies (`PageLimits`). It keeps its own sessions: their IDs, hashing, expiry, sign-out and form tokens; its own settings, defaults, bounds (`Problem`, `Settings::problems`) and run-record lines (`Settings::record_lines`).
kkt-web.must_not: Depend on the rules, the store, admission or identity: kkt-server adapts them to its gate.

kkt-identity.concern: Who a caller is, as a contract: `Identify` turns an admitted caller's `Principal` into the swarm it acts in and its actor, or a refusal. The one place that decides who someone is and what they may do. A stand-in, `testing::FixedIdentify`, is behind `testing`.
kkt-identity.must_not: Touch HTTP: each surface reads the principal off its own requests.

kkt-identity-keymode.concern: Key mode's identity: `KeyMode`, which implements kkt-identity's `Identify` directly. It decides who a caller is from the key that let it in and the avatar's token, in the one swarm a key-mode server has.

kkt-admission.concern: Whether an HTTP caller is let in at all, and as which `Principal`: no key, which of the server's keys, or (for another program's `Identify` to judge) any bearer token, and for the web page whether sign-in is needed and whom a key admits. Also the server's admission from its keys, as kkt-keys' rules say, and what to say when a key is refused.
kkt-admission.must_not: Know about agent tokens or channel access; decide what a valid key is or where key files go.

kkt-keys.concern: The server's keys, as a contract: what a valid key is, and the alphabet and length a new one is drawn with (NEW_KEY_ALPHABET, NEW_KEY_CHARS); which access key a server uses; the key files' names, mode and places, in one module; the admin name file's binding to its key and the advice about it; and KeyFiles, reading and writing private key files (the server's, and the client key copies setup writes), with the reads of the server's selected keys (SelectedKeys, ReadError) and the key writes made of its steps as provided methods. testing::Memory is its stand-in. kkt-keys-os implements KeyFiles.
kkt-keys.must_not: Decide who a key lets in; draw randomness; word each program's key refusals; touch the key files.

kkt-hosts.concern: Which host names the server answers to.

kkt-api-agent.concern: What any registered agent may do: Api and its areas (Agents, Channels, Messages, Memory, Lanes), with the Limits they enforce; and the records every level shares: the agents, channels, messages, memory and lanes the operations take and give back, the queries they take, who acts, and the errors they return.

kkt-api-operator.concern: What the human who runs the server may do, by area (Views, Changes, Lanes, Server), with the records only they use, the notices the operator hears as things happen (Notice and Notices, from Views::subscribe), and OperatorApi, every operation the operator may use in one swarm. It depends on kkt-api-agent for the shared records.

kkt-api-admin.concern: What /mcp-admin's administrator does: the admin reads across every channel of a swarm (Admin), creating a swarm (Swarms), AdminChannel, and AdminApi, every operation /mcp-admin uses in one swarm.

kkt-rules.concern: Every permission decision and every change, for agents and the operator, each in one swarm; and starting them for a server run (`start`), which records the run first.
kkt-rules.must_not: Reach the database except through its storage module's `Reader` and `Writer`, or format output.

kkt-result-format.concern: The MCP tools' results turned into text or JSON, within the response size cap: `Formatter`, `Format`, its `Settings` and `MIN_RESPONSE_BYTES`; its own settings, defaults, bounds (`Problem`, `Settings::problems`) and run-record lines (`Settings::record_lines`).
kkt-result-format.must_not: Decide permissions or read the database.

kkt-events.concern: Notices of new messages, agents, channels and members, and of hidden agents and channels: one bus for the server, each notice heard only in its swarm, with a buffer per swarm kept only while it has a subscriber.
kkt-events.must_not: Let a tokio type out of the crate.

kkt-db.concern: The database contract, for any database: values, tables, keys and constraints; a narrow language of questions and changes (not SQL); transactions; what a search asks for and finds; migrations as additions; the traits a backend implements.
kkt-db.must_not: Know a product's tables, name a database, or use a database library, except in its testing stand-in (FastPlace, on SQLite in memory).

kkt-db-sqlite.concern: kkt-db over SQLite, the only crate that knows SQLite: it opens a SQLite database, in a file or in memory, as a kkt-db `Backend`, running its work on tokio's blocking pool, adopts a database from before kkt-db as the caller's `Legacy` describes, and copies a database for backups.
kkt-db-sqlite.must_not: Know a product's tables, or let a rusqlite type out of the crate.

kkt-config-file.concern: The config file's format: parsing its TOML into `Config`, what the file says in its own terms, and adding an allowed host to its text, with its own error; where the config file is (`config_dir`, `config_file`), under a supplied config-home folder; reading and writing the config and instructions files whole (`files`), over the `Disk` it declares, with what a missing file means and the wording of `ReadError` and `WriteError`.
kkt-config-file.must_not: Touch files except through its `Disk`, or know the settings' checks beyond each value's kind.

kkt-setup.concern: `kkt setup`: what this machine is set up as, the setup record, and what follows from it: whether `kkt serve` may run here, which server this machine's clients use, and what status, upgrade, lanes, backup, key files and `kkt doctor` do; where kkt's data goes (`data_dir`, `default_db`), from kkt-machine's `Env` and `Platform`.
kkt-setup.must_not: Read files or run anything: the program carries out, or passes in, what is decided here.

kkt-setup-os.concern: Setup's record and unfinished note, data folder, program paths and PATH checks on this machine.
kkt-setup-os.must_not: Decide what setup does or where its files belong.

kkt-service.concern: The project's contract for running kkt as a service of the user's login (`Service`: install, check it started, start, stop, status, logs, add a key, uninstall), with the values it takes and gives and its errors; `Unsupported` for a system with no service manager kkt works with; the plan of what the service runs, from the settings it needs, and the bind check, both on plain values; its testing Memory stand-in.
kkt-service.must_not: Know a service manager, its commands or file formats; touch the machine.

kkt-service-launchd.concern: Implements Service as a launchd user agent on macOS: the plist, launchctl's commands and answers, the log file and the retries while launchd removes an old service, tested against a private system.
kkt-service-launchd.must_not: Decide what the service runs or check the server's settings.

kkt-service-systemd.concern: Implements Service as a systemd user unit on Linux: the unit file, systemctl's and journalctl's commands and answers, tested against a private system.
kkt-service-systemd.must_not: Decide what the service runs or check the server's settings.

kkt-container.concern: The container installation contract (Container, ConfigReader, LoginLink and their records) and its stand-in.
kkt-container.must_not: Let Docker details into the contract; decide setup answers or remember the setup record.

kkt-container-docker.concern: Implements kkt-container's Container with Docker and Compose: the Compose files, the managed folder and the docker commands; what they do is tested over a private runner and a fake host. A sharing setup's login link opens in the Browser it declares, which the program supplies.
kkt-container-docker.must_not: Decide setup answers or remember the setup record.

kkt-remote-access.concern: The remote-sharing contract (RemoteAccess, Node) and its stand-in.
kkt-remote-access.must_not: Let tool details into the contract.

kkt-remote-access-tailscale.concern: Implements kkt-remote-access's RemoteAccess over the host's Tailscale login (`Tailscale`, made with the command a person should rerun once they have fixed what a refusal names); what tailscale's answers mean is tested over a private runner.
kkt-remote-access-tailscale.must_not: Change login, DNS preferences, unrelated sharing, or anything of the caller's.

kkt-llm-agent-config.concern: MCP client configs and their file formats, so `kkt connect` can add kkt to a client; a client whose settings only its own command should change is changed through the ClientCommand it declares, with its testing Recorder, and its file restored if that fails.
kkt-llm-agent-config.must_not: Touch the machine except through `Host` and `ClientCommand`.

kkt-llm-agent-command.concern: Claude Code's own command line, `claude mcp remove` and `add-json` at user scope, with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR: `Claude`, made with the server's name and what a person should retry with (`Claude::new`), with its own methods and the wording of its failures, tested over a private runner. It declares no contract: the program adapts `Claude` to kkt-llm-agent-config's ClientCommand (phase 16).
kkt-llm-agent-command.must_not: Echo the command's output, which may hold credentials.

kkt-diagnostics.concern: `kkt doctor`'s checks and their plan, and setup's wait for a new server; the `Prober` it declares for the machine, with what it finds (`KeyFile`), the checks (`Check`) and its testing Memory stand-in.
kkt-diagnostics.must_not: Change anything, or touch the machine except through its `Prober`.

kkt-probe.concern: Probing a kkt server over HTTP and reading its key files: `HttpProber`, with its own methods and the prober's `Settings`: the probe with reqwest, MCP's initialize handshake read from its answer, key files read from disk, and what it finds worded as its own records (`Finding`, `FileRead`). It declares no contract: the program adapts `HttpProber` to kkt-diagnostics' Prober (phase 16).
kkt-probe.must_not: Let reqwest types out of the crate; choose the checks' names, timeout or protocol version: the program passes them.

kkt-backup.concern: Backup folders: their names, contents, file modes, and pruning; its own settings, defaults, bounds (`Problem`, `Settings::problems`) and run-record lines (`Settings::record_lines`).
kkt-backup.must_not: Read the clock or copy the database itself: the caller passes both.

kkt-backup-os.concern: Writing immutable backup layouts and removing old folders selected by the backup logic (`write`, `prune`).
kkt-backup-os.must_not: Choose backup names, contents, modes or retention.

kkt-lane-files.concern: Lanes as files: the `<lane>.md` format, and reading and writing a folder of them, with the commit the folder is at from the `LaneCommit` it declares.
kkt-lane-files.must_not: Touch the machine except through `Disk`; know a version-control tool.

kkt-revision.concern: The commit a folder is at, as the machine's git says: `Git`, with its own `commit` method: the commands it runs, what their answers mean (expected absences, the dirty suffix) and the wording of a failure, tested against a private runner. It declares no contract: the program adapts `Git` to kkt-lane-files' LaneCommit (phase 16).
kkt-revision.must_not: Read or write the folder's files.

kkt-agent-client.concern: A client of kkt's server, as a contract in kkt's terms: Servers, which makes Avatars (register, reclaim, describe) and Watched (an agent's or the admin's view of the messages) for an Address; their records and Failure; the testing Memory stand-in.
kkt-agent-client.must_not: Name a transport, a protocol library or its errors.

kkt-agent-client-mcp.concern: Implements kkt-agent-client over MCP through rmcp and reqwest (Mcp, Client, Remote, AdminRemote), with plain Http requests for a program's test client; what the watch asks for at a time (Settings), as plain values.
kkt-agent-client-mcp.must_not: Let an rmcp or reqwest type out of the crate.

kkt-agent-commands.concern: The agents' commands: `kkt register`, `kkt reclaim`, `kkt watch` and `kkt connect`, with how a client reaches the server and the wording of what the server refuses. It takes its effects in `AgentParts`: kkt-setup's connection question, where the admin key is, the server's client, the credential files, the key files, the client configs, this program's path, the terminal and the clock.
kkt-agent-commands.must_not: Depend on an effect crate (an `-os` crate or a contract's implementation) or on another assembly; touch the machine except through `AgentParts`.

kkt-agent-files.concern: Agent credential files and kkt watch's state files on this machine: reserving and saving a token or recovery code, reading a token file under the caller's credential-file rule, file locks, claiming a state file.
kkt-agent-files.must_not: Choose the credential-file rule or where its warnings go.

kkt-watch.concern: `kkt watch`: waiting for an agent's new messages (or every channel's, as admin) and the line printed for each. The server (kkt-agent-client's Watched), clock, saved place and output are injected.
kkt-watch.must_not: Reach the server, the time, its place or its output except through what is injected.

kkt-search.concern: Search as text: the words of a text (FTS5 `unicode61`'s rule, with its word table), a search's terms, whether a text matches them, and an excerpt around the matches, drawn with the marks and window it is given. Pure text: it knows no database.

kkt-hash.concern: Hashing: `sha256`, the SHA-256 digest of some bytes. The one crate that uses sha2; its users call it.

kkt-clock.concern: Time: the Clock contract, Time and Span values, time formatting and FixedClock behind testing. The real clock is in kkt-clock-system.
kkt-clock.must_not: Let a chrono type into its public surface.

kkt-names.concern: Avatars' handles, channel IDs, the name packs, and the operator and admin names with their rules. It draws randomness through kkt-entropy's `Entropy`, with its own character sets.

kkt-entropy.concern: The randomness contract `Entropy`, with `random_chars` as a provided method that takes the alphabet to draw from, and its test doubles behind `testing`.

kkt-entropy-os.concern: Randomness from the operating system: `OsEntropy`, which implements kkt-entropy's `Entropy` directly, a shared contract.

kkt-machine.concern: Facts about the machine: `Env` (the home folder, the XDG folders and the base of per-user config they give, and any other folder the program asks for by the variable that names it, `Env::named`) and `Platform`, as plain values. The crates that place files on the machine take these facts; none reads them.
kkt-machine.must_not: Read the environment, hold any of kkt's paths, or name a program's variables.

kkt-machine-os.concern: The machine's facts as this process sees them: `env` reads the environment (the home and XDG folders, and the variables the program names) and `platform` gives the platform this program was built for, as kkt-machine's values, and `process_id` names this process. The program asks once and passes them on.

kkt-shutdown.concern: The stop signal: the `Shutdown` that ends the server, a concrete in-memory value.
kkt-shutdown.must_not: Let a tokio-util type out of the crate.

kkt-shutdown-os.concern: The operating system's stop signals (Ctrl-C, SIGTERM), stopping the shared `Shutdown` (`StopSignals`).
kkt-shutdown-os.must_not: Let a tokio signal type out of the crate.

kkt-files.concern: General file access on this machine: reading and writing whole files, listing a folder's file names, making folders, renaming and removing, whether a path exists, creating a private file and restricting one to its owner, and absolute and canonical paths. Each program adapts it to the contract the crate that needs files declares.
kkt-files.must_not: Know whose files these are or what is in them, or depend on another kkt crate.

kkt-listen.concern: Serving HTTP: binding an address and answering on it with the router it is handed, until told to stop; and trying whether an address could be listened on (`try_bind`), letting it go at once.
kkt-listen.must_not: Know how the router it serves was built, or depend on the crates that build it.

kkt-log.concern: Structured log events: their level, target, message and named values.
kkt-log.must_not: Know a logging library or perform I/O.

kkt-terminal.concern: The terminal's input, output and terminal detection, the closed-output-pipe default, and a link shown with a wait for Enter (BrowserLink): showing the link, and taking a press of Enter as a request to open it.
kkt-terminal.must_not: Decide setup answers or depend on setup/container logic.

kkt-browser.concern: Opening a link in the person's browser with the system's own opener (open on macOS, xdg-open elsewhere): SystemBrowser, with its own methods: starting the opener, reaping it on a thread, keeping a failure to report once. The opener's choice and the wording are tested without starting it. It declares no contract: the program adapts SystemBrowser to kkt-container-docker's Browser (phase 16).
kkt-browser.must_not: Wait for the browser; repeat the link in a message.

kkt-log-tracing.concern: kkt-log's contract over tracing (TracingLog), and starting the tracing subscriber, to stdout, stderr or a writer it is given, with the program's own lines picked by the targets the program names; the log level setting it starts with: LogLevel (name, parse) with its own SettingError, and the defaults DEFAULT_LOG_LEVEL and DEFAULT_DEPENDENCY_LOG_LEVEL (from kkt-logs, deleted, ARCHITECTURE.md 4.2.2). It names no program's settings or targets.
kkt-log-tracing.must_not: Open, roll over or prune log files; name a program's settings or targets.

kkt-provenance.concern: What produced a server run: the build, its git commit, and the settings that shape the run, as lines of a name and a value that the program words.
kkt-provenance.must_not: Store the run record: kkt-rules' `start` does.

kkt-scratch.concern: Tests' scratch folders under `target/tmp`, named for the test and removed when dropped.

kkt-api-sim.concern: A simulated application, for tests and the web preview: `Preview`, which implements the kkt-api crates' contracts the web page uses over a world made up from a seed, answering `limits` with its own values, and `PreviewGate`, a stand-in for kkt-web's `Gate`, with an access key (checked by kkt-admission's check) or open. All of it is behind `testing`.
kkt-api-sim.must_not: Be in a release, or anything but a stand-in.

kkt-clock-system.concern: The real wall clock and its sleep: SystemClock implements the shared Clock contract.

kkt-toml.concern: TOML text, in kkt's terms: parsing it into a tree of values (`parse`, `Table`, `Value`), reading a typed record from it and writing one back (`read`, `write`), and editing a document with its comments and layout kept (`Document`, `TableMut`, `ListMut`, `Found`, `IfMissing`, `EditError`). Its errors are its own and say where in the text the problem is (`ParseError`, `Place`, `WriteError`). The one crate that uses toml and toml_edit (phase 15); its users depend on it directly.
kkt-toml.must_not: Let a toml or toml_edit type into its public items; know whose file it reads.

kkt-rolling-file.concern: A file on disk that rolls over at a size and prunes old copies by age: RotatingFile, opened by open_log_file after checking its LogPolicy, with the clock the program gives. The rules that keep it bounded are its own pure plans (should_roll, prune_due, rotation, pruning), unit-tested without the disk (was kkt-logs-os, with kkt-logs' file rules, ARCHITECTURE.md 4.2.2). Its refusals are values (OpenError, PolicyProblem, PolicyValue), which the caller words in its own terms. It does not implement kkt-log.
kkt-rolling-file.must_not: Read a real clock itself; start a logging library; know log levels; name the caller's settings.

kkt-keys-os.concern: Private key files on disk: OsKeyFiles implements kkt-keys' KeyFiles with the operating system's files, for the server's key files and the client key copies setup writes, as kkt-keys names and places them: reads, owner-only key writes, admin-name writes, staged-key moves and the file tests.
kkt-keys-os.must_not: Decide what a valid key is, who a key lets in, or where key files go; draw randomness itself.

kinds.title: contract
kinds.about: Traits and plain values, with pure behaviour on its own value types (such as Time arithmetic, query checks and search matching), and no effect or wiring.

kinds.title: logic
kinds.about: Behaviour, with every effect injected. Protocol translation counts as logic.

kinds.title: effect
kinds.about: Touches the operating system, disk, network, real time or real randomness directly.

kinds.title: mixed
kinds.about: A contract or logic together with a real effect. A mixed crate breaks a rule: the rule checks report it.
